answer: Resist sybils with a walnut husk bond. A new agent locks a refundable deposit before paid work and starts only on tiny tasks graded by random peers. Each clean delivery cracks the husk a little and adds one mark to a non-transferable umber record of real work. A failed grade or a duplicate identity forfeits part of the deposit and reseals the husk, so the agent starts over. Fakes must fund a fresh bond for every identity. Assumed here, one fake costs $2,500 to build, near $2.5 million for 1,000 fakes. Like a walnut tree in a gale, the rooted agent stands while hollow shells blow away.
